plan.chapterName: OpenStax Calculus, chapter 12: Vectors in Space
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional construction drawn in the first octant that locates a single point three different ways at once. The vertical axis is labeled z, the axis running to the right is labeled y, and the axis coming toward the viewer at the lower left is labeled x. A filled black dot at the upper right is tagged by two stacked lines of text, P(x, y, z) on top and P(rho, theta, phi) beneath it. A solid blue segment runs from the origin out to the dot and is labeled rho along its length. A small arc near the origin between the z-axis and that segment is labeled phi. Dashed orange lines complete the rest of the construction: a vertical drop from the point down to the xy-plane labeled z, and a segment from the origin across the xy-plane to the foot of that drop labeled r, with a small square where they meet marking the right angle. A second arc at the origin, between the x-axis and the segment r, is labeled theta. Superimposing all three descriptions on one point exposes theta and r as the quantities the systems share. The drawing introduces the ordered triple (rho, theta, phi), in which one distance and two angles fix a location in space.

elements: z-axis pointing straight up, labeled z
y-axis pointing to the right, labeled y
x-axis angled toward the viewer at lower left, labeled x
filled black point P in the first octant
stacked two-line label: 'P(x, y, z)' above 'P(ρ, θ, φ)'
solid blue radial segment from origin to P, labeled ρ
arc at the origin between the z-axis and the radial segment, labeled φ
arc at the origin between the x-axis and the ground-projection segment, labeled θ
dashed orange vertical drop from P to the xy-plane, labeled z
dashed orange segment in the xy-plane from origin to the foot of the drop, labeled r
small right-angle square where the vertical drop meets the ground segment

interactions.label: ρ (radial distance)
interactions.teaches: ρ stretches the point radially from the origin — it is the straight-line distance to P, not the ground projection

interactions.label: θ (azimuth)
interactions.teaches: θ rotates the ground projection r around the z-axis — this angle is shared by both cylindrical and spherical systems

interactions.label: φ (polar angle from z-axis)
interactions.teaches: φ tilts P down from the z-axis; small φ keeps P near the z-axis while φ near 90° puts it in the xy-plane

interactions.label: Coordinate readout
interactions.teaches: The same fixed point is described three ways; switching readouts highlights which components are shared (θ, and r = ρ sin φ) and which are system-specific

demo_steps.title: Spherical description
demo_steps.narration: With the spherical readout active, ρ, θ, and φ are highlighted: one distance from the origin plus two angles fix P. Note the φ arc measured down from the z-axis and the θ arc in the xy-plane.

demo_steps.title: Change the polar angle
demo_steps.narration: Reduce φ toward 20°. P swings up toward the z-axis: the vertical height z = ρ cos φ grows while the ground projection r = ρ sin φ shrinks.

demo_steps.title: Same point, cylindrical readout
demo_steps.narration: Switch to cylindrical. The point does not move — only the description changes: r, θ, z are highlighted, showing θ and the geometry of r and z are shared between systems.

demo_steps.title: Rectangular readout
demo_steps.narration: Switch to rectangular: x = ρ sin φ cos θ, y = ρ sin φ sin θ, z = ρ cos φ. All three descriptions name the same dot in space.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes span ~7 world units each: +Z screen-up, +Y screen-right, +X angled down-left toward viewer (matching the source orientation — note y goes right and x comes forward, a left-handed-looking but standard OpenStax layout; keep labels exactly as in source). Point P computed as x = ρ sin φ cos θ, y = ρ sin φ sin θ, z = ρ cos φ with ρ=4, θ=40°, φ=50° by default, placing P in the first octant upper-right as in the source. Radial segment solid blue #1a5caa, radius ~0.03, with label ρ midway. Point P black sphere radius 0.09. Dashed orange #e07b2a lines: vertical drop from P to (x, y, 0) labeled z, ground segment from origin to (x, y, 0) labeled r. Right-angle square (~0.25 units) at the foot of the drop. φ arc (radius ~1.2) between +Z axis and radial segment; θ arc (radius ~1.2) in xy-plane between +X axis and ground segment; both as thin curved lines near the origin with italic labels. Two-line point label 'P(x, y, z)' / 'P(ρ, θ, φ)' to the right of P.
interactionPlan.notes: Recompute P, all segments, and both arcs reactively on every slider change; arcs can be built as Line segments sampled along the angle. For the coordinate-system toggle, highlight the relevant labels/elements (emissive boost or color) and show a small numeric readout panel of the active triple — the point itself never moves when toggling. Allow theta to wrap 0–360 so P can leave the first octant, which helps show the angles are general, though the default view matches the source figure. Thin grey dashed helper lines from P to each axis in rectangular mode are optional but aid the (x,y,z) reading.

authoredContext:
In the spherical coordinate system, a point P in space (the figure) is represented by the ordered triple (ρ,θ,φ) where

In the Cartesian coordinate system, the location of a point in space is described using an ordered triple in which each coordinate represents a distance. In the cylindrical coordinate system, location of a point in space is described using two distances (randz) and an angle measure (θ). In the spherical coordinate system, we again use an ordered triple to describe the location of a point in space. In this case, the triple describes one distance and two angles. Spherical coordinates make it simple to describe a sphere, just as cylindrical coordinates make it easy to describe a cylinder. Grid lines for spherical coordinates are based on angle measures, like those for polar coordinates.

The relationship among spherical, rectangular, and cylindrical coordinates.

This figure is the first quadrant of the 3-dimensional coordinate system. It has a point labeled “(x, y, z) = (rho, theta, phi).” There is a line segment from the origin to the point. It is labeled “rho.” The angle between this line segment and the z-axis is phi. There is a line segment in the x y-plane from the origin to the shadow of the point. This segment is labeled “r.” The angle between the x-axis and r is theta.

By convention, the origin is represented as (0,0,0) in spherical coordinates.

interactions.teaches: φ tilts P down from the z-axis; small φ keeps P near the z-axis while φ near 90° puts it in the xy-plane

interactions.label: Coordinate readout
interactions.teaches: The same fixed point is described three ways; switching readouts highlights which components are shared (θ, and r = ρ sin φ) and which are system-specific

demo_steps.title: Spherical description
demo_steps.narration: With the spherical readout active, ρ, θ, and φ are highlighted: one distance from the origin plus two angles fix P. Note the φ arc measured down from the z-axis and the θ arc in the xy-plane.

demo_steps.title: Change the polar angle
demo_steps.narration: Reduce φ toward 20°. P swings up toward the z-axis: the vertical height z = ρ cos φ grows while the ground projection r = ρ sin φ shrinks.

demo_steps.title: Same point, cylindrical readout
demo_steps.narration: Switch to cylindrical. The point does not move — only the description changes: r, θ, z are highlighted, showing θ and the geometry of r and z are shared between systems.

demo_steps.title: Rectangular readout
demo_steps.narration: Switch to rectangular: x = ρ sin φ cos θ, y = ρ sin φ sin θ, z = ρ cos φ. All three descriptions name the same dot in space.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes span ~7 world units each: +Z screen-up, +Y screen-right, +X angled down-left toward viewer (matching the source orientation — note y goes right and x comes forward, a left-handed-looking but standard OpenStax layout; keep labels exactly as in source). Point P computed as x = ρ sin φ cos θ, y = ρ sin φ sin θ, z = ρ cos φ with ρ=4, θ=40°, φ=50° by default, placing P in the first octant upper-right as in the source. Radial segment solid blue #1a5caa, radius ~0.03, with label ρ midway. Point P black sphere radius 0.09. Dashed orange #e07b2a lines: vertical drop from P to (x, y, 0) labeled z, ground segment from origin to (x, y, 0) labeled r. Right-angle square (~0.25 units) at the foot of the drop. φ arc (radius ~1.2) between +Z axis and radial segment; θ arc (radius ~1.2) in xy-plane between +X axis and ground segment; both as thin curved lines near the origin with italic labels. Two-line point label 'P(x, y, z)' / 'P(ρ, θ, φ)' to the right of P.
interactionPlan.notes: Recompute P, all segments, and both arcs reactively on every slider change; arcs can be built as Line segments sampled along the angle. For the coordinate-system toggle, highlight the relevant labels/elements (emissive boost or color) and show a small numeric readout panel of the active triple — the point itself never moves when toggling. Allow theta to wrap 0–360 so P can leave the first octant, which helps show the angles are general, though the default view matches the source figure. Thin grey dashed helper lines from P to each axis in rectangular mode are optional but aid the (x,y,z) reading.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional construction drawn in the first octant that locates a single point three different ways at once. The vertical axis is labeled z, the axis running to the right is labeled y, and the axis coming toward the viewer at the lower left is labeled x. A filled black dot at the upper right is tagged by two stacked lines of text, P(x, y, z) on top and P(rho, theta, phi) beneath it. A solid blue segment runs from the origin out to the dot and is labeled rho along its length. A small arc near the origin between the z-axis and that segment is labeled phi. Dashed orange lines complete the rest of the construction: a vertical drop from the point down to the xy-plane labeled z, and a segment from the origin across the xy-plane to the foot of that drop labeled r, with a small square where they meet marking the right angle. A second arc at the origin, between the x-axis and the segment r, is labeled theta. Superimposing all three descriptions on one point exposes theta and r as the quantities the systems share. The drawing introduces the ordered triple (rho, theta, phi), in which one distance and two angles fix a location in space.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rho, theta, and phi: the learner adjusts each coordinate, the point P moves while the radial segment, ground projection, vertical height, and angle arcs update, showing how one distance and two angles determine a 3D location.
- Toggle between rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical readouts: the learner switches coordinate systems, the same point remains fixed while x,y,z, r,theta,z, and rho,theta,phi components highlight, making clear which quantities are shared and which are system-specific.
plan.sourcePath: OpenStax Calculus, chapter 12: Vectors in Space

discrepancies: The ρ line is drawn as a thick blue rod, noticeably heavier than the thin blue line in the source
The source's z-axis arrow and label sit directly above the origin with the φ arc clearly nested between z-axis and ρ; in the render the φ arc/label is small and cramped near the origin

evaluation.notes: A faithful and pedagogically strong spherical-coordinates figure with correct geometry, labels, and rich interactions; only minor stylistic deviations (thick ρ rod, cramped angle arcs) distinguish it from the source.
action_items: Thin the ρ cylinder slightly to better match the source's single-stroke blue line
Increase the radius/legibility of the φ and θ arcs and their arrowheads so the angle annotations read as clearly as in the source
Lengthen the axes modestly so the composition breathes like the source figure
